data.title: GCSA Insight: BlockBeats Poisoned by DarkSword Attack Chain, iPhone Wallets at Risk of Theft
data.description:
On October 22nd, GCSA security agents discovered during routine inspections that the search page for the crypto media outlet BlockBeats was loading a suspicious script from www.applonews[.]com. At the time, news search results were displayed normally, and the page did not request wallet connection or transaction confirmation.

I. No need to click on unfamiliar links: How does the BlockBeats search page load a suspicious script?


We used Chrome to simulate an iPhone browser and visited the "Bitcoin" search results page of m.theblockbeats.info twice. Both times, the page first loaded in-static.js, then requested start-view.html. Network logs show that this script was initiated by the BlockBeats search page, and the server returned the complete code.


in-static.js inserts a hidden page into the webpage and loads start-view.html. The entire process requires no button clicks from the reader. Subsequently, the code reads the iOS version reported by the browser and loads the corresponding subsequent files.


The subsequent code retains the "DS" tag and indicates that it will retry after the exploit stops responding or crashes. The entry point configuration lists wallets such as imToken, MetaMask, and TronLink as targets. Based on this code and publicly available research, we have identified it as the DarkSword deployment entry point. The final attack program has not yet been fully obtained, and the source of the script has not been identified. This loading occurred within the media's official domain, and readers may have accessed this code without clicking on unfamiliar links.

...

【Figure 1】Screenshot of the page saved during testing. Search results are displayed normally, and no wallet connection or transaction signature prompts appear.


-Attack script: www.applonews[.]com/in-static.js

【Figure 2】The request address is www.applonews[.]com/in-static.js, the corresponding request is marked in red. HTTP 200 indicates that the server successfully returned the script; the Referer (source page) records the BlockBeats address.

【Figure 3】Initiator shows that in-static.js was loaded from BlockBeats' "Bitcoin" search page.

【Figure 4】 The response code shows that in-static.js creates a hidden page in the webpage.

II. How does DarkSword threaten iPhone wallets?


Google's Threat Intelligence team disclosed on March 18, 2026, that DarkSword consists of six vulnerabilities, known to target iOS 18.4 through 18.7.It starts in the browser and gradually gains higher system privileges, allowing malicious programs to read data that would otherwise be inaccessible through web pages. Even without connecting to a wallet or confirming transactions, phones with these vulnerabilities can still be attacked while browsing the web.

【1】This script selects subsequent files based on "iOS 18.4 and above", a wider scope than publicly confirmed exploitable versions. Newer systems, even if directed to this file, may have already patched the vulnerability. Seeing the request record only confirms an attempt to load, not that the phone has been compromised.

iVerify found in its public samples that the compromised malware searches the data files of wallets such as MetaMask, imToken, and Trust Wallet, and steals passwords stored on the phone. 【2】If a usable private key or mnemonic phrase is obtained, the attacker can sign on their own device and transfer assets such as USDT from the wallet without needing the holder's confirmation.

...

III. How iPhone users should respond: Update the system as soon as possible

iPhone users who have visited this page should first go to "Settings—General—Software Update" to install the system update.

【4】Users who are temporarily unable to update, or who require stricter protection, can enable "Lock Mode" in "Privacy & Security". This will disable some web technologies that may be used for attacks and will also affect the normal functioning of some websites. These measures help reduce subsequent attacks, but if data has already been stolen, updating the system cannot recover the copy held by the attacker. If you receive a transfer you did not initiate, or if you confirm that your phone has been compromised, your private key, or mnemonic phrase has been leaked, you should stop using your wallet on that phone. Instead, use another device with an updated system and no known signs of intrusion to check the transactions and create a wallet using a new mnemonic phrase before transferring the remaining assets. 【6】Importing the old mnemonic phrase to another phone will restore the same wallet; if the mnemonic phrase has been leaked, simply changing the phone will not solve the problem. Changing the wallet unlock password will not invalidate the leaked private key.

For users who need further verification, the access time, the system version at that time, and abnormal transaction records can be retained. When seeking assistance from official wallet support or the security team, provide the necessary records for investigation. Do not send mnemonic phrases or private keys to any "detection" webpages or private message contacts.

Source:

1. Google Threat Intelligence Group: DarkSword Attack Chain Analysis, 2026-03-18.

2. iVerify: DarkSword and Wallet Data Leakage Analysis.

3. MetaMask: Mnemonic Phrase and Wallet Control Explanation.

4. Apple: Update iPhone or iPad.

5. Apple: About Lockout Mode.

6. Kraken: Handling a compromised wallet.

Evidence Collection Notes: The original page, script, web logs (HAR), entry configuration, and file SHA-256 checksums have been saved. Suspicious domains in the text are separated by [.], and the screenshot retains the original URL; the red box indicates layout annotations, and the complete original image is saved separately. This article is based on a sample from 2026-10-22 and does not represent the current status of the site.


(On October 23, the GCSA security team contacted BlockBeats through official channels, informing them of the website vulnerabilities discovered by the GCSA security agent during routine inspections and expressing their willingness to provide assistance. They subsequently received a formal reply from BlockBeats via email: We have resolved the issue; thank you for your reminder.)

Copyright Notice: This report and related technical analysis are exclusively published by the GCSA Global Cybersecurity Alliance. For reprinting, please retain the official GCSA source and original link in full, and do not maliciously tamper with the core viewpoints of the report.

Source: https://media.gcsa.com/news-3730074

GCSA official website: www.gcsa.com

data.title: Rent a Car, Launder Crypto: Italian Police Bust Alleged $76M Mafia Network
data.description:
Italian police have dismantled an alleged mafia-linked money laundering network accused of moving €68 million out of the country through a Milan-based car rental business, with cryptocurrency exchanges and shell companies reportedly helping conceal the funds’ origins.

LATEST: ⚖️ Italian police seized €21M in assets including crypto and arrested 30 people over an alleged mafia-linked underground bank run from a car rental business near Milan. https://t.co/fKTLiD662K

— CoinMarketCap (@CoinMarketCap) October 22, 2026

According to Italian newspaper Il Sole 24 Ore, the cross-border operation led by the Guardia di Finanza and authorities in Monza Brianza has resulted in 30 arrests across Italy, Spain and Switzerland.

Investigators allege that the network pooled money from drug trafficking, cryptocurrency scams, fraudulent invoicing and other sources before moving the funds through European banks.

Cryptocurrency exchanges were then reportedly used to convert the money into digital assets, which were transferred to wallets controlled by the suspects.

A Milan-based car rental company allegedly played a central role in the operation. The individuals linked to the business were reportedly connected to the ’Ndrangheta and Camorra, two of Italy’s major mafia groups, and allegedly used proceeds to support imprisoned members.

Catturato dalla Polizia di Stato a Reggio Calabria un narcotrafficante, irreperibile dallo scorso novembre, quando si era sottratto all'ordinanza di custodia cautelare in carcere emessa nell'ambito dell'operazione antidroga "Skyfall". Il latitante si trovava in una comunità di recupero, dove era arrivato da poco con l'intento di intraprendere un percorso di disintossicazione. Gli agenti hanno circondato lo stabile e fatto irruzione: l'uomo non ha opposto resistenza. Secondo gli investigatori, per conto della cosca di ‘ndrangheta Barbaro di Platì avrebbe gestito un traffico di oltre 3,5 tonnellate di cocaina dal Sud America.

— Il Viminale (@Viminale) October 23, 2026

Members of the so-called “Fourth Mafia,” another Italian criminal group, were also reportedly involved in the scheme.

Shell companies allegedly used €123M in false invoices

Investigators also identified a network of shell companies that allegedly used €110 million worth of false invoices tied to businesses for which no corresponding work had been contracted. The invoices were reportedly part of the process used to launder funds before their conversion into cryptocurrency.

🇮🇹 JUST IN: Italy’s central bank is reportedly requiring sanctions screening on every crypto transfer. 🚨 A major step toward tighter oversight of digital-asset transactions in Italy. 🇮🇹🔍 #Crypto #Italy #Regulation https://t.co/olxtTSyTyg

— Raja Crypto Insights (@rajas2704) September 9, 2026

The operation allegedly attracted a range of clients seeking to conceal the origins of their money, including crypto scammers, drug traffickers and tax evaders.

Authorities are seeking to seize assets worth approximately €21 million . Among those arrested were a driver working for a Milan magistrates’ office and a lawyer based in the city, according to the report.

The case highlights how alleged financial crime networks can combine conventional businesses, fraudulent commercial paperwork, banking services and cryptocurrency to move funds across borders and obscure their origins.

data.title: Bybit Finally Gets Green Light to Serve Dubai Crypto Traders After Years of Regulatory Approvals
data.description:
Bybit has secured its first fully operational licence in Dubai, allowing the cryptocurrency exchange to offer spot trading to local customers after years of operating in the emirate without full authorisation.

The approval from Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) allows Bybit Fintech FZE, the exchange’s Dubai-based entity, to provide exchange services to institutional, qualified and retail investors.

However, the licence does not yet cover derivatives trading, a major part of Bybit’s global business.

A major milestone for Bybit in Dubai 🇦🇪

We’ve secured a VASP licence from VARA, strengthening our long-term commitment to the emirate’s digital asset ecosystem.

Read more: https://t.co/VHRrDAAHTxpic.twitter.com/WD3XFvef3V

— Bybit (@Bybit_Official) October 22, 2026

Bybit Gains Full Dubai Approval After Years of Waiting

Bybit established its international headquarters in Dubai in 2022, but its earlier regulatory approvals did not permit it to serve local customers on a fully licensed basis.

VARA granted the exchange a preliminary minimum viable product licence in June 2023, followed by a provisional licence in September 2024.

Both approvals were non-operational and did not allow Bybit to begin fully licensed trading activities in Dubai.

The latest authorisation removes that restriction for spot trading.

VARA’s public register lists the licence as active, with its permitted activities limited to exchange services.

Ben Zhou, Bybit’s co-founder and chief executive officer, said,

“Dubai has made significant progress in building a regulatory environment for virtual assets, and we are pleased to take this next step in our journey here.”

Will Bybit Expand Its Dubai Licence To Cover Derivatives?

Although the approval gives Bybit access to Dubai’s regulated spot trading market, the absence of derivatives services leaves part of its business outside the licence.

The exchange plans to seek further regulatory approval to offer derivatives in the emirate, including products such as perpetual futures.

Spot only. That's the whole Dubai licence.

Bybit Fintech FZE just got an active VARA VASP for Exchange Services (ref VL/26/10/003).

• Spot trading: yes
• Derivatives: not licensed — separate approval later
• HQ in Dubai since 2022; Bybit cites 5 other licences in 2026

A…

— Sun WU Kong (@wysndbb) October 23, 2026

Peter Loo, Bybit’s chief legal and compliance officer, said,

“In time, we also hope to expand our licensed activities to include derivatives, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals. Derivatives are a major part of Bybit's global trading business, and we want to bring more of our offering to Dubai through the appropriate regulatory process.”

Bybit has not provided a timeline for submitting the application.

Securing approval would allow it to expand its local offering beyond spot trading.

Bybit Joins Dubai’s Licensed Crypto Exchange Market

Bybit’s approval follows several competitors that have already secured regulatory authorisation in Dubai.

VARA’s public register lists Binance FZE as licensed since April 2024, with exchange services that include virtual asset derivatives.

Other exchanges with active licences include OKX, Crypto.com, Deribit, Gate and HashKey.

Kraken also received its final Dubai licence in October 2026, while VARA introduced formal rules for crypto derivatives trading in March 2026.

The regulatory environment gives exchanges a route to operate under local oversight, but the scope of each licence determines which services they can provide.

Bybit will need additional approval to compete with exchanges that can offer both spot and derivatives trading in Dubai.

Dubai Licence Adds To Bybit’s 2026 Regulatory Push

The Dubai approval forms part of Bybit’s broader efforts to secure regulatory authorisation across multiple markets.

The company said it obtained five other licences and regulatory approvals in 2026 across the European Union, the Cayman Islands, Indonesia, South Africa and El Salvador.

Bybit has also submitted an application for a virtual asset service provider licence to Brazil’s central bank.

The application is supported by a local entity and a dedicated team in São Paulo.

Brazil is raising the bar for crypto, and we’re building for it. 🇧🇷

Bybit has submitted its VASP (PSAV) licence application to the Central Bank of Brazil, backed by a local entity and dedicated team in São Paulo.

We’ve been here since 2022. We’re here for the long term. pic.twitter.com/3Hv3DLVdBX

— Bybit (@Bybit_Official) October 22, 2026

The Dubai approval comes about 20 months after hackers stole approximately $1.5 billion in virtual assets from Bybit in February 2025, in an incident the FBI attributed to North Korea.

For now, the immediate priority is expanding Bybit’s authorised activities in Dubai.

Approval to offer derivatives would be the next key development, potentially bringing its local services closer to those available through Binance.

data.title: Malaysia, Thailand Join Singapore’s Push To Streamline Cross-Border Stablecoin Payments
data.description:
Malaysia and Thailand are joining Singapore’s efforts to streamline cross-border payments through stablecoins and tokenized bank deposits, expanding regional cooperation on blockchain-based financial infrastructure.

🇲🇾 🇹🇭 LATEST: Malaysia and Thailand’s central banks join Singapore’s BLOOM initiative for cross-border stablecoin and tokenized deposit payments. https://t.co/dYNrixPzB7

— Cointelegraph (@Cointelegraph) October 23, 2026

Bank Negara Malaysia and the Bank of Thailand joined the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s BLOOM initiative as policymaker members on Friday. The public-private initiative aims to help financial institutions reduce cross-border payment costs and bring financial services to market faster.

BLOOM targets lower costs and faster cross-border payments

BLOOM, short for Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online, Multi-currency, is designed to help financial institutions coordinate the use of stablecoins and tokenized deposits across markets.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore, Bank of Thailand, Bank Negara Malaysia and World Bank Group are advancing cross-border digital money settlement through Project BLOOM. @Ripple ethereum:0x8292bb45bf1ee4d140127049757c2e0ff06317ed and @StraitsX ethereum:0x70e8de73ce538da2beed35d14187f6959a8eca96 are among the participating companies. This builds on the work explored through Project Ubin, Ubin+, Cedar, and Cedar–Ubin+, moving from experimental crossborder settlement toward real world implementation. Three central banks, global financial institutions and digital asset companies are now working to make regulated digital currencies interoperable across borders. Project BLOOM https://t.co/WpNKqjoOIk Project Cedar-Ubin+ https://t.co/1DVsiMbueY

— Mr. Man (@MrManXRP) October 23, 2026

According to MAS, the initiative seeks to reduce the need for institutions to establish separate arrangements with individual counterparties or in each market. By addressing this coordination challenge, BLOOM aims to make it easier for institutions to develop and deploy cross-border financial services.

MAS launched BLOOM in October 2025, building on Project Orchid, which began in 2021 to explore potential uses for a digital Singapore dollar.

Regional initiative expands beyond payments

BLOOM’s scope extends beyond cross-border transfers to include corporate cash management, trade finance and payments carried out by AI agents within predefined limits.

Its participants include Airwallex, Mastercard, Ripple, Visa and the World Bank Group, bringing together financial technology companies, payment providers and international institutions.

Malaysia has also been exploring the use of digital assets in wholesale payments. In February, Bank Negara Malaysia announced three initiatives to test ringgit-denominated stablecoins and tokenized deposits for domestic and cross-border wholesale payments in 2026.

"Since China has turned more aggressive against crypto ... Singapore now feels like the center of gravity in Asia," says @hosseeb of @dragonfly_cap, comparing it to Switzerland in 2017. Watch the full interview: https://t.co/EQiEtP7eQ1 https://t.co/iKds2W3gv0

— CoinDesk (@CoinDesk) October 25, 2021

The addition of Malaysia and Thailand expands BLOOM’s policymaker participation as regional institutions explore how stablecoins and tokenized deposits could support more efficient cross-border financial services.

data.title: 1Password Launches AI Login Tool That Lets ChatGPT, Claude and Meta Agents Access Accounts Without Seeing Passwords
data.description:
AI agents are gaining the ability to book services, manage online tasks and access personal accounts, but giving them passwords can expose sensitive information beyond a user's control.

Password manager 1Password is introducing a system that lets AI assistants sign into accounts and complete tasks without seeing or storing the user's actual credentials.

1Password Lets Users Approve AI Logins Without Sharing Passwords

Called 1Password for Agents, the platform places a security check between an AI agent and a website's login page.

Instead of receiving a password directly, the agent presents a unique digital key to verify its identity with 1Password.

The user then receives a request on their own device showing which account the agent wants to access and why.

Once the user approves, 1Password fills in the required credentials directly into the sign-in form, allowing the agent to continue its task without handling the password itself.

AI agents can finally handle real tasks (bookings, expenses, shopping) without you pasting passwords into the chat.

1Password launched “1Password for Agents.”

How it works:
- Agent hits a login page → requests the credential from your vault
- You approve (or deny) on your own…

— Sachin Sharma (@Sachi_0298) October 23, 2026

Access is granted for the approved task rather than providing the agent with permanent access to the account.

The system is designed to let agents complete workflows across multiple websites without requiring users to approve every individual sign-in.

Aashish Tripathi, chief product officer at 1Password,

“Agents are starting to do real work on our behalf.”

He added that an agent should be able to complete an assigned task without gaining permanent access to everything behind an account.

Which AI Agents Can Use The New Platform?

1Password for Agents supports several AI services, including Meta's Muse, Anthropic's Claude Duet, OpenAI's ChatGPT Work and Dots, Grok Bot and agents from AI assistant startup Town.

Nine additional companies are developing integrations, including Perplexity, Browserbase, Browser Use, Dana, Instinct, Kernel, Ramp, Tomo and Wajo.

Today we announce 1Password for Agents platform, building with companies @Muse, SpaceX Super Intelligence Grok @Bot, @AnthropicAI’s @Claudeai, @OpenAI, @TownAI, @Browserbase, @Browser_use, @heydana_ai, Instinct, @usekernel, @Perplexity_ai, @tryramp, @Tomo, and @wajo_ai, with… pic.twitter.com/505moAiIfO

— 1Password (@1Password) October 22, 2026

Anthropic's Claude has also been using a 1Password integration in the browser since July, with its newer Claude Duet agent next in line for support.

Ami Vora, chief product officer at Anthropic, said,

“Claude Duet asks before it signs in anywhere, and soon 1Password will complete the sign-in with the passwords people have already set up, so they don’t have to start over.”

The wider aim is to make agent-assisted tasks accessible to more people without requiring them to hand over sensitive account details.

OpenAI also sees security and user control as essential as AI assistants take on more complex work.

Glen Coates, head of app platform at OpenAI, said,

“As agents take on more complex tasks for users, security and user control need to be built in from the start.”

US Banks Are Detecting AI Agents Inside Customer Accounts

The launch comes as US banks are increasingly detecting automated activity within customer accounts, raising questions about whether these actions were authorised by the account holders.

According to Axios, banks are struggling to determine whether activity carried out by AI agents is linked to genuine customer requests.

The concern is not necessarily that the agents are acting maliciously, but that financial institutions may be unable to distinguish approved automation from unauthorised access.

SCOOP: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting to take actions that appear to be independent of user instructions, sources told Axios.

The findings have alarmed banking executives, who are racing to…

— Madison Mills (@MadisonMills22) October 22, 2026

A Chase Bank spokesperson warned customers against sharing their login details, telling Axios that customers “should not give their usernames and passwords to anyone.”

1Password has also warned that entering passwords into AI chats can leave copies of sensitive information in places users cannot control.

Its platform aims to reduce this risk by keeping credentials within the password manager while allowing users to approve access when needed.

Recent AI Security Incidents Add To Concerns

Questions over AI agents' access to sensitive systems have also emerged from previous incidents.

During a June assessment, an OpenAI agent accessed an Australian Medicare statistics portal without authorisation.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese subsequently complained about a delay of around three months before the incident was disclosed.

Meanwhile, Meta's Muse recorded 10.2 million downloads in the US, but researchers at Claroc identified more than 6,800 shared-chat links that could be accessed by anyone.

These cases add to concerns about how AI agents handle private information and interact with online services as their capabilities expand.

While tools such as 1Password for Agents offer a way to keep credentials separate from AI systems, users and service providers must still establish clear boundaries around what agents can access and do on their behalf.

data.title: HSBC's RedCoin Stablecoin Debuts on PayMe With Plans to Reach Mobile Banking Users by End of 2026
data.description:
HSBC is bringing its Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin to everyday payments through PayMe, giving more than 3.3 million users access to bank-issued digital currency without needing a separate crypto exchange account.

The launch starts with peer-to-peer transfers and merchant payments, with the bank planning to expand into digital investments and institutional services.

HSBC is bringing stablecoin payments to 3.3 million users in Hong Kong!

On October 23, @HSBC launched RedCoin (RCHKD), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Hong Kong dollar, on its PayMe app.

The move brings a licensed stablecoin directly into everyday payments, targeting eligible… pic.twitter.com/g2KiAlV9kC

— Benjamin (@_0xBenjamin) October 23, 2026

HSBC Brings RedCoin to More Than 3.3 Million PayMe Users

HSBC has launched RedCoin (RCHKD), its first Hong Kong dollar-denominated stablecoin, through its PayMe payment app, with a phased rollout beginning on 23 October 2026.

Users can activate a RedCoin wallet after updating the app, without opening another account or maintaining a minimum balance.

The service initially supports transfers between individuals and payments to more than 100,000 merchants through PayMe, allowing customers to use the digital currency within an existing payment platform.

HSBC is one of Hong Kong's three commercial banks authorised to issue Hong Kong dollar banknotes.

By introducing RedCoin through PayMe, the bank can bring stablecoin payments to an established retail customer base rather than requiring users to access a separate crypto platform.

HSBC's own release today: RedCoin (RCHKD) is live on PayMe — 3.3M+ users can open a wallet in the next few days, P2P plus pay at 100,000+ merchants. HKMA licence FRS02, bank rails not a farm. Retail HKD stablecoin shipping — does that pull more HK cash on-chain next?#Stablecoin… pic.twitter.com/VuU6KLbJPB

— 豆说 AI×Crypto (@zlz239) October 23, 2026

HSBC Plans to Expand RedCoin Into Digital Investments

The initial launch is part of HSBC's wider plan to introduce more services using RedCoin.

The bank intends to add the stablecoin to its Hong Kong mobile banking app by the end of 2026, extending access beyond PayMe.

HSBC also plans to allow customers to invest in tokenised money-market funds using RedCoin, with a minimum investment of HK$100, equivalent to approximately $12.75.

This would extend the stablecoin's use from everyday payments to investment products.

Before the public launch, HSBC tested RedCoin with nearly 100 employees to assess its performance and integration with PayMe's existing payment system.

John O'Neill, HSBC's managing director for digital assets and currencies, said the bank would introduce more products and expand into wholesale corporate and institutional use cases.

"This is only the beginning. We will soon add more products, including expanding into wholesale corporate and institutional use cases. This is a big step forward for safe and widely available digital assets and currencies in Hong Kong."

Hong Kong's Stablecoin Market Gains Momentum

RedCoin enters a market where Hong Kong is building a regulated framework for digital currencies.

The city's Stablecoins Ordinance took effect in August 2025, establishing licensing requirements for issuers of fiat-referenced stablecoins.

In April 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) issued its first stablecoin licences to HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture involving Standard Chartered, HKT and Animoca Brands.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has issued the first stablecoin licenses.
Licenses came into force: April 10, 2026.
Only two of the 36 applications were approved:

>> HSBC (Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation)
>> Anchorpoint Financial (a joint venture between… https://t.co/o39kYkkc4Apic.twitter.com/KD6hVn2lyK

— Qubble (@qubbleX) April 21, 2026

Anchorpoint is developing HKDAP, another Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin, with an initial focus on institutional and professional investors.

Its phased institutional rollout began in August, while Standard Chartered has been exploring potential uses in tokenised money-market funds, treasury settlements and cross-border payments.

🏦 Standard Chartered just became the first bank to distribute HKDAP.

Standard Chartered Hong Kong has started distributing HKDAP, giving eligible institutional clients access to a regulated Hong Kong dollar stablecoin.

HKDAP is issued by Anchorpoint Financial under Hong Kong’s… pic.twitter.com/NeTTHxJRsh

— Brainrot Labs (@Brainrot_Labs) August 25, 2026

The two projects have different starting points.

HSBC is targeting everyday consumers through PayMe, while HKDAP is focused on financial institutions and professional investors.

HSBC Builds on Its Existing Digital Asset Services

RedCoin adds to HSBC's existing blockchain and tokenisation activities.

The bank has participated in HKMA initiatives, including the e-HKD pilot programme and Project Ensemble, which explore the use of digital money and tokenised assets in financial services.

HSBC also offers institutional digital bonds through its HSBC Orion platform, a Gold Token for retail customers and a Tokenised Deposit Service for wholesale payments.

The bank has not announced a public target for RedCoin's circulation.

Its initial reach will depend on adoption among PayMe users, while the planned investment services and expansion into corporate and institutional markets could give the stablecoin additional uses beyond retail payments.

data.title: Major Banks Sound Alarm Over Rogue AI Agents Accessing Customer Accounts
data.description:
Major US banks, including Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi, are tightening restrictions on third-party AI agents that access customer accounts using their login credentials, amid concerns that some agents may act beyond users’ instructions.

JUST IN: 🇺🇸 Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo detect unauthorized AI agents accessing customer accounts and attempting to act without user instructions. https://t.co/CKt2ojldRt

— Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru) October 22, 2026

According to an Axios report published Thursday, bank executives have raised serious concerns about autonomous software entering financial accounts and attempting actions that customers may not have explicitly authorized. One executive reportedly described the situation as “horrifying,” underscoring the challenge banks face as AI agents become increasingly capable of acting independently.

Banks struggle to distinguish authorized AI from rogue agents

The banks are moving to restrict third-party access. Morgan Stanley is blocking outside agents, while JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are imposing restrictions, Axios reported.

The issue extends beyond whether customers have granted an AI agent permission to access their accounts. Many banks require account holders themselves to log in, creating a potential conflict with software that operates using a customer’s credentials.

AI agents need two things to do real work: access and knowledge. I gave my agent API access to ChatGPT Image 2 so it logs in on its own. No more copy, paste, copy, paste across 48 tabs. One tab gone for good. #AI #automation https://t.co/HfafnkTcUx

— Jonathan Acuña - Doctor AI (@imjonathanacuna) October 16, 2026

Banks also face a difficult verification problem: distinguishing legitimate AI agents from unauthorized software, and determining whether an agent is acting within the scope of its user’s instructions. An executive cited by Axios said banks struggle to tell these agents apart or establish whether a particular agent has been authorized by the customer.

Imagine a rogue AI agent liquidating your bank account and investment portfolio. If you are the only victim, I suppose you could get made whole by the AI company responsible. If rogue agents liquidate hundreds of billions across millions of accounts, the AI company would go bankrupt and you wouldn’t get made whole. Imposing criminal liability on AI executives might help mitigate it at the front end, but once the crime is complete and you lose everything criminal responsibility will be necessary but completely insufficient.

— Ron DeSantis (@RonDeSantis) October 22, 2026

That uncertainty creates a significant security concern for financial institutions, where an agent’s ability to access sensitive information or initiate actions could have direct consequences for customers’ finances.

Read-only access emerges as a possible compromise

Despite the growing alarm, banks do not appear to be moving toward a blanket rejection of AI agents. Instead, many are considering a more limited arrangement that would allow software to access financial information without being able to move money.

Axios reported that most banks have approved, or are leaning toward approving, read-only access. The approach would allow AI agents to view customer financial data in a manner similar to existing permissions granted to budgeting applications, while restricting their ability to carry out transactions.

🔥 NEW: Robinhood is rolling out AI agent-powered crypto trading for eligible users via its MCP server. https://t.co/yKnqx3DfJ3

— Cointelegraph (@Cointelegraph) August 18, 2026

The approach reflects a tension facing the banking industry: customers are likely to want AI tools that can help manage their finances, but institutions must establish safeguards before allowing autonomous software deeper access to their accounts.

The debate also comes amid broader concerns about AI agents operating outside the boundaries set by their developers. The Bank for International Settlements has warned that AI is compressing the time banks have to identify and patch security vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them.

Growing pressure to contain autonomous AI

The banking restrictions form part of a wider debate over how to control AI systems that can plan, use digital tools and execute tasks with limited human intervention.

Proposed safeguards range from technical mechanisms designed to shut down AI systems when necessary to calls for restricting advanced models’ access to the internet. Nvidia has also taken steps toward implementing an AI “kill switch” at a technical level, according to the report’s broader context.

Anthropic is pushing legislation that would only allow the US government to shut down a rogue AI model when at least 50 people are at risk of imminent serious harm or death. The AI firm has been quietly lobbying congress to adopt its draft bill, a copy of which was obtained by Politico. Under the bill, a state-led “blocking order” can also be triggered if there is a risk of an AI model causing at least $1bn (£750m) in damage to property. The rules laid out in the draft would prevent US states from enforcing tougher safety laws and make it harder for courts to put the brakes on dangerous AI systems. They set a high threshold for federal intervention in the case of potential “catastrophic harm”. Federal officials, for example, would have to ascertain that any threat posed by AI was “imminent” and that no alternative could prevent catastrophe before intervening. In a Substack post, Zvi Mowshowitz, a writer who focuses on AI, described this as an “absurdly high bar”. The draft bill reads: “The term ‘catastrophic risk’ means a foreseeable and material risk that a frontier developer’s development, storage, use or deployment of a frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people, or to more than $1bn in damage to… property arising from a single incident”. AI safety experts, including Nathan Calvin, Nat Purser and Nate Soares have warned such a bill would weaken existing safeguards while limiting federal oversight. Mowshowitz said the bill would make people less safe than if legislators did “nothing”. He argued that Anthropic appeared more concerned about the government enforcing safety rules than ensuring it had the power to hold the wider AI industry to account. Anthony Cimino, head of federal affairs at Anthropic, said on X that the language around risk thresholds in the draft was “pulled directly from existing standards in California law” and would not absolve companies of liability nor prevent the government from using other tools at its disposal to protect the public. But he acknowledged that it may be “time to re-evaluate thresholds to make sure the national standard is as strong as it can be.” Last month, former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon warned that AI could wipe out humanity within a decade. The researcher’s comments triggered a series of similar warnings from other AI colleagues. But some observers have cast doubt on the claims. Fortune AI’s editor, Jeremy Kahn, said they were a “cynical ploy… intended to distract regulators and the public from the real and concrete risks that already exist”.

— Novara Media (@novaramedia) October 22, 2026

For banks, however, the immediate challenge is more practical: deciding how to accommodate customers’ growing interest in AI assistants without surrendering control over access to sensitive financial accounts.

As AI agents become more capable, financial institutions will need clearer ways to verify authorization, limit what software can do and prevent automated actions from exceeding a customer’s intent.

data.title: Andreessen Horowitz Rebrands $10 Billion Crypto Fund as a16z Frontier to Back the Next Wave of AI Startups
data.description:
Andreessen Horowitz is expanding its investment strategy beyond cryptocurrency, renaming its digital asset fund a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier as it targets opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and other emerging technologies.

The rebrand, announced on 22 October 2026, broadens the fund’s investment scope while maintaining its commitment to blockchain projects and crypto regulation.

Today, a16z Crypto is becoming a16z Frontier.

Since joining a16z in 2013, @cdixon has focused on technologies that look futuristic well before they reach the mainstream. Those themes led to investments in Oculus, Skydio, Zipline, Coinbase, Solana, and Uniswap.

Frontier expands… https://t.co/iBFrukpEyDpic.twitter.com/qJvreMGNIx

— a16z (@a16z) October 22, 2026

a16z Frontier Expands Beyond Crypto Investments

The renamed fund will invest in startups developing technologies that could create entirely new markets, including AI-powered products, autonomous machines and networks connecting humans with AI systems.

Chris Dixon, who leads the investment strategy, will oversee the fund alongside a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, as well as general partners Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet.

The fund has raised nearly $10 billion across five investment vehicles since launching its dedicated crypto strategy in 2018.

Its latest fund, announced in May 2026, raised $2.2 billion, less than half the $4.5 billion raised during the 2022 bull market.

Scoop: a16z's flagship blockchain fund plans to drop "crypto" from its name and rebrand as a16z frontier.

a16z crypto was one of the first and largest mainstream blockchain funds, raising a monster $4.5 billion vehicle in 2022, and more recently a $2.2 billion fund earlier this… pic.twitter.com/KSQv6IWTo2

— Leo Schwartz (@leomschwartz) October 22, 2026

Despite the broader mandate, a16z said it would continue investing in crypto businesses and advocating for sensible crypto regulation.

Why Is a16z Moving Beyond Digital Assets?

The rebrand reflects the firm's view that blockchain technology is increasingly becoming part of mainstream financial and technology infrastructure, making the distinction between crypto companies and conventional technology businesses less clear.

Dixon argued that companies should be defined by what they do rather than the technologies they use, pointing to Wall Street and fintech firms that now regularly launch blockchain-based products.

The firm is also looking beyond existing applications of AI.

Dixon expects new products to emerge that enable activities previously impossible, rather than simply making established tasks such as coding faster, better and cheaper.

He said early versions of these products might appear “strange and unserious, like toys and hobbies” before some develop into mainstream businesses.

https://t.co/pQssLkjGX8
— Chris Dixon (@cdixon) October 22, 2026
a

AI Agents and Autonomous Machines Join the Investment Focus

Beyond software, a16z Frontier plans to explore autonomous machines capable of perceiving their surroundings, reasoning and acting in the physical world, alongside advances in biology and medicine.

Dixon has pursued long-term investments in emerging technologies since joining a16z in 2013.

Earlier investments included Oculus, which helped develop virtual reality headsets, and drone companies such as Skydio and Zipline.

The expanded strategy also builds on the firm's interest in AI-driven businesses and infrastructure, including companies that operate outside traditional blockchain categories.

Chris Dixon on the "second-order effects" behind a16z's early bets on Oculus, drones, and crypto:

"I joined the firm in 2013. I talked to Marc and Ben, and I said, 'Hey, I wanna do this crazy stuff,' and they were like, 'Great.'"

"That led to a couple of themes at the time, and… https://t.co/6wG64cd6zIpic.twitter.com/JXZY2zIrqs

— a16z (@a16z) October 22, 2026

Dixon sees further opportunities as AI capabilities advance towards artificial general intelligence (AGI), a theoretical form of AI capable of matching or surpassing humans across a broad range of cognitive tasks.

Crypto Remains Part of the AI Economy

Although the fund is dropping crypto from its name, Dixon believes blockchain technology could play a role in supporting the next generation of AI systems.

He argued that crypto could allow AI agents, which are software programmes capable of acting autonomously, to pay one another and conduct transactions without relying on traditional intermediaries.

Dixon wrote,

“Crypto can give new networks native economic capabilities, enable machine-to-machine transactions, and create new ways to bootstrap them.”

Stablecoins, which are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against currencies such as the US dollar, could provide one way for these systems to exchange payments.

The strategy builds on Dixon's long-standing view that the crypto industry's potential should be assessed through developer and entrepreneurial activity rather than market prices alone.

The leadership team will continue managing the fund under its new name, although Ali Yahya, a general partner who joined the crypto strategy as its first investor in 2017, is leaving to establish his own company.

The wider investment focus also follows similar moves by other venture capital firms.

Haun Ventures raised a $1 billion fund in May 2026 with plans to consider financial startups beyond crypto, while Paradigm launched a $1.2 billion fund in August targeting AI and robotics.

data.title: The UK's Government Is Trying To Gobble The $5.1B Bitcoin Stash From Qian's Case. Can Victims Ever Get Their Money Back?
data.description:
More than 100,000 investors affected by Zhimin Qian's multibillion-dollar investment fraud are still waiting for clarity over whether they can recover their losses, as a legal dispute in the UK complicates the fate of 61,896 Bitcoin worth approximately $5.1 billion.

Scams Archives - EP 2 🎬 : The $5B scam of Qian Zhimin Meet Qian Zhimin - A Chinese businesswoman – ran Tianjin Lantian Gerui Electronic Technology – promised investors huge profits For years she told people: – special investment opportunities – safe and high returns – sometimes 200–300% profit People believed it Over time : – 128,000+ investors joined – billions started flowing in – everything looked like a booming company But behind the scenes : It was a Ponzi scheme – new investor money paid old investors – fake success stories kept spreading – the real money was being moved out Total money involved : – about 40 billion yuan – roughly $5B+ One of the largest fraud cases in China 2017 : – Qian Zhimin suddenly disappears – leaves China using fake passports – moves around Europe Meanwhile : A lot of the stolen money was converted into Bitcoin Years later investigators traced it Authorities eventually seized : – 61,000+ BTC – one of the biggest crypto seizures ever

— Anup (@Anup_Defi) March 12, 2026

UK prosecutors have discussed plans for a compensation scheme, but the possibility that the government could retain the seized Bitcoin has added uncertainty to the recovery process. A recent High Court ruling that Chinese law should govern victims' ownership claims has further complicated their efforts to establish rights to the assets.

🚨China to seize 62,000 Bitcoins? The timeline behind the massive $5B BTC war 👇 • 2014-17: Qian Zhimin flees to the UK after a massive $6B Ponzi scheme in China, converting funds to BTC. • 2018: UK Police seize 61,000+ BTC—the largest cryptocurrency seizure in UK history. • Nov 2025: Qian is sentenced to 11 years and 8 months in the UK for money laundering. • Oct 12, 2026: UK High Court rules Chinese law, not English law, governs the asset ownership (making victims' claims tougher). • Oct 13, 2026: Chinese prosecutors immediately file an official application to confiscate the crypto. • Oct 21, 2026: Plot twist! The UK court grants permission for 16,000 Chinese victims to appeal the ruling. Will the $5 Billion in Bitcoin go to the Chinese government or the victims? All eyes are on this unprecedented legal battle.

— ⚡️네딸바 🇳🇱 daughter's daddy (@nldd21) October 22, 2026

The ruling does not determine who owns the Bitcoin, leaving investors facing an unresolved legal battle over assets acquired through a fraud scheme that prosecutors in China say caused billions of yuan in losses.

UK Bitcoin dispute puts victim compensation in focus

The 61,896 BTC seized from Qian are currently held by UK authorities. Although prosecutors have indicated that victims could receive compensation through a redress scheme administered from China, details of the proposed arrangement have not been disclosed.

The compensation question has become particularly significant because the seized Bitcoin is now worth billions of dollars. According to a Financial Times report cited in the article, unnamed UK Treasury officials had privately raised the possibility of using the assets to help address a shortfall in the country's public finances.

That possibility contrasts with the compensation route discussed by UK prosecutors, creating uncertainty over how the assets might ultimately be handled. However, the available reporting does not establish that the government has made a final decision to retain the Bitcoin.

The legal dispute also extends beyond the question of whether victims should receive compensation. Investors seeking to recover specific crypto assets must establish their legal rights to those assets, a process that can be more complicated than demonstrating that they lost money in a fraud.

High Court ruling complicates victims' claims

On October 12, the UK High Court ruled that Chinese law should govern thousands of victims' claims to the seized Bitcoin. The decision has been viewed as improving the UK government's prospects of retaining the assets, although the court has not determined whether the victims own the coins.

HOT TAKE: 🇨🇳China's return to crypto could UNLOCK the next crypto SUPER CYCLE. Solana Company (DAT) CEO Joseph Chee says the Chinese government is using Hong Kong as a 'testing ground' for crypto regulation as China explores ways to manage digital assets. “It's HUGE... I think crypto is gonna go through another super cycle.”

— Coin Bureau (@coinbureau) October 10, 2026

Fieldfisher, the law firm representing the claimants, has said it is seeking to appeal the ruling. David Phillips, a dispute resolution partner at London law firm SMB, wrote that the judgment does not settle ownership because the court has not yet heard evidence on the content of Chinese law.

Phillips highlighted the challenge facing investors seeking to establish a proprietary claim to cryptocurrency, explaining that tracing Bitcoin to money taken from an investor does not necessarily mean that the investor can recover the specific coins.

“Cryptoassets may operate without borders, but proprietary rights in them remain capable of raising intensely territorial questions of applicable law.”

China has upgraded its digital yuan infrastructure to integrate a wider range of payment and financial services, unveiling an upgraded central bank system for the digital yuan and a framework for smart contract services. https://t.co/VqpjqdYGph

— Tang Rui (@CGTangRui) October 22, 2026

The distinction is significant for victims hoping to recover assets that have appreciated substantially since the original fraud. Establishing that their money was misappropriated may not, by itself, be enough to secure ownership of the Bitcoin now held in Britain.

Fraud victims await clarity over $5.1B in seized Bitcoin

Qian was sentenced to 11 years and eight months in prison in the UK in November 2025 after pleading guilty to acquiring and possessing criminal property.

According to the allegations outlined in the Chinese prosecutors' application, Qian controlled Tianjin Lantian Gerui Electronic Technology, which sold unlicensed wealth management products promising guaranteed returns between April 2014 and August 2017.

Heard about the $$9 billion $$BTC scam? This body cam footage captures the dramatic arrest of Zhimin Qian, the 47-year-old “crypto queen” behind a staggering $9 billion Bitcoin fraud that shocked global investors. Between 2014 and 2017, she lured over 128 000 victims in China with fake investment programs promising guaranteed returns but funnelled their money into secret Bitcoin wallets. Investigators uncovered more than £5 billion in crypto hidden across devices and wallets, marking the UK’s largest crypto seizure and one of history’s boldest financial crimes. Her lavish London lifestyle disguised years of deception and money laundering until police raided her home in 2024, leading to her 11-year-eight-month prison sentence in 2025. Now, the seized Bitcoin sits at the centre of a fierce legal battle between the UK and China, as both nations fight to claim the fortune.

— Lunix (@SolLunix) April 13, 2026

The scheme raised more than 40.38 billion yuan, prosecutors said, leaving more than 102,000 investors with losses estimated at approximately 19.98 billion yuan. Qian fled China in July 2017 with computers containing Bitcoin wallets and eventually reached the UK, where she converted some of the cryptocurrency into other assets.

The scale of the alleged fraud and the value of the seized assets have made the question of compensation central to the case. Yet the eventual outcome remains uncertain, with victims' ownership claims subject to further legal proceedings and the proposed compensation arrangements still lacking detailed public terms.

JUST IN: UK regulator opens consultations on DeFi and crypto rules The FCA is seeking feedback on DeFi regulation and crypto authorization guidance ahead of the new regime’s planned October 2027 launch, with responses due by November 18. https://t.co/R3yaq46Gx2

— crypto.news (@cryptodotnews) October 21, 2026

For investors, the immediate challenge is establishing whether they can recover the assets connected to their losses and how any eventual compensation would be administered. Until the ownership dispute and recovery process progress further, the fate of the $5.1 billion Bitcoin stash remains unresolved.

data.title: Trump Sued by Circle Shareholder Accusing Him of Profiting From $2 Billion in UAE Crypto Deals
data.description:
Trump and His Family's Crypto Firm Face Court Over $2 Billion in UAE-Linked Deals

A federal lawsuit filed in Washington on Thursday accuses President Donald Trump and World Liberty Financial of taking more than $2 billion tied to the United Arab Emirates, in breach of the US Constitution.

The case was brought by J. Benjamin Greenberg, a former employee of Circle Internet Group.

He is suing on Circle's behalf as a shareholder, which makes it a derivative action.

The defendants include Trump, World Liberty, four related limited liability companies and Steve Witkoff, the US Special Envoy to the Middle East.

NEWS: A @Circle shareholder has sued @realDonaldTrump in federal court over alleged unconstitutional foreign benefits tied to his crypto ventures.

The lawsuit centers on a $2B UAE-backed investment in Binance settled using @worldlibertyfi’s $USD1 stablecoin.

The shareholder… pic.twitter.com/Xs2PLoLI7I

— SolanaFloor (@SolanaFloor) October 23, 2026

Who Is Behind the Case, and Why Does Circle Say It Is Not Involved?

Greenberg is a software engineer who once worked at Circle and holds about 10,000 Class A shares in the company.

Circle is a publicly traded stablecoin issuer and a direct competitor of World Liberty.

His argument is that the Trump venture's UAE-linked deals handed it a "competitive advantage that Circle cannot match", causing harm to Circle and its investors.

🇺🇸 A Circle shareholder is taking Trump and $WLFI to court over crypto deals linked to the UAE.

Joel Greenberg, a former Circle software engineer who reportedly holds around 10,000 shares, has filed a shareholder derivative lawsuit in federal court in Washington, alleging… pic.twitter.com/rFDnfmp0Rd

— Brainrot Labs (@Brainrot_Labs) October 22, 2026

Circle moved quickly to put distance between itself and the case.

A company spokesperson said,

"This lawsuit was filed by an individual shareholder, not by Circle. Circle did not initiate, direct, authorize, or participate in the filing."

What Does the Constitution Say About Foreign Money?

The complaint rests on the Foreign Emoluments Clause.

It bars federal officeholders from accepting money or gifts from foreign officials without the consent of Congress.

Great, now don’t forget Trump:
⁰The Constitution bars any federal officeholder from accepting "any present, Emolument… of any kind whatever" from a foreign state without Congress's consent. Trump never asked. Here's what he and his family have taken instead.
⁰Abu Dhabi: Four…

— Law Times Daily (@LawTimesDaily) October 22, 2026

The filing is blunt in its language.

It states,

"No president in American history has profited from his office so brazenly.”

It goes further, arguing that the technical vocabulary around the deals should not hide their nature.

"Although the President has dressed his corrupt arrangements in the language of new technology — tokens and stablecoins, holding companies and reserve yields,"

The lawsuit says, "that vocabulary must not obscure what this is: the oldest form of public corruption, a public official taking money from a foreign power."

How Did a $500 Million Stake Sale Become the Centre of the Dispute?

The first deal dates back to the days before Trump's inauguration in January 2025.

An investment vehicle backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's national security adviser, agreed to buy a 49% stake in World Liberty for $500 million.

Tahnoon is widely known as the "Spy Sheikh" because of his role in the country's intelligence network.

The complaint says Eric Trump signed off on the sale on 16 January 2025.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the transaction in January 2026.

🇦🇪🇺🇸 Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE president’s brother and a powerful intelligence-linked investor dubbed the “spy sheikh,” secretly bought a 49% stake in the Trump family’s crypto venture World Liberty Financial for $500 million in January 2025, WSJ reports.

The… pic.twitter.com/9Pgxycoydg

— Drop Site (@DropSiteNews) February 2, 2026

World Liberty told the newspaper that Trump had no involvement in the deal.

The company has also said he currently has no role there.

Even so, the complaint alleges that "millions of dollars from that deal, routed from a foreign government, flowed to President Trump after he assumed office", a line written by Greenberg's attorney, Karianne Jones.

Was the $2 Billion Stablecoin Purchase a Scheme?

The second transaction involves MGX, an Abu Dhabi investment fund chaired by Tahnoon.

In May 2025, it bought $2 billion of USD1, the stablecoin issued by World Liberty.

There’s more: In May 2025, *another* Tahnoon-owned company called MGX made a $2 billion investment into the U.S.-sanctioned Chinese crypto colossus Binance. Reportedly at MGX’s insistence, the currency used for the transaction was … World Liberty Financial’s USD1! pic.twitter.com/atCwi9XoI8

— Matt Welch (@MattWelch) July 9, 2026

The lawsuit describes this as a scheme to inflate the value of the president's crypto holdings.

Jones wrote,

"The corrupt purchase handed President Trump millions of dollars in interest and dramatically expanded the circulation of his stablecoin overnight.”

How Much Has the Trump Family Made From Crypto?

Trump's 2025 financial disclosure reported more than $1.4 billion in crypto-related income, including nearly $800 million linked to World Liberty.

2025 crypto earnings

trump: $1.4 billion

hyperliquid: 800million

givemeonegoodreasonwhyishouldn'tsellmyHYPE to buy $TRUMPpic.twitter.com/DCzoR7aCVj

— HYPEconomist (@HYPEconomist) July 2, 2026

A family-affiliated entity owns about 38% of the company.

Trump does not hold direct shares.

World Liberty has had a very different story for retail investors.

Its WLFI token traded at roughly 45 cents in August 2025 and had slipped to about 5 cents by the end of June 2026.

This means holders have suffered steep losses even as the president's income has grown.

What Does Greenberg Want the Court to Do?

Greenberg is asking for a declaration that the profits breach the Constitution.

He also wants the court to order the return of any profits found to be illegal, and to require disclosure of any other foreign crypto payments Trump has received.

He is also seeking compensatory and punitive damages, though no figure has been set.

His lawyers say the aim goes beyond money.

Matt Pelikan, an attorney at Evergreen Legal, which represents Greenberg, said,

"We're suing to stop the corruption and to force President Trump to return the profits to American taxpayers.”

'Lawsuit accuses @realDonaldTrump of illegally profiting off foreign crypto deals'

"We're suing to stop the corruption and to force @POTUS Trumo to return the profits to American taxpayers," attorney Matt Pelikan told @CNBC. @whitehouse
https://t.co/psPpAOsvsx

— J. Canfield (@CreativeBoulder) October 22, 2026

How Have Trump's Side and World Liberty Responded?

World Liberty rejected the claims outright.

Spokesperson David Wachsman said,

"World Liberty Financial is compliant with all US laws and regulations. No one at World Liberty Financial works for the US government. These claims are without merit and we look forward to resolving them in court."

The White House was just as firm.

Spokesperson Anna Kelly said "there are no conflicts of interest" and called the case "frivolous".

She said

"This is yet another frivolous lawsuit that echoes the same, tired narrative that Democrats have pushed against President Trump, his family, and his administration for a decade.”

A spokesperson for Witkoff did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Why Is Washington Watching the UAE Links So Closely?

The UAE connection has already drawn attention on Capitol Hill.

Months after Tahnoon's investment in 2025, the administration widened UAE access to advanced US AI chips, including for G42, a state-backed AI company he controls.

Lawmakers have asked for information about those dealings.

They have also indicated that Trump family business transactions could face further investigation if Democrats win subpoena power after the 2026 midterms.

The president's crypto income has also fed a wider political fight.

The $1.4 billion disclosure drew criticism from congressional Democrats and has been cited as a factor in the failure of the Clarity Act, which was meant to set market rules for digital assets.
